newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK business sees rights shrinking after 1997 - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK business sees rights shrinking after 1997 - poll.

text.p: Most businessmen in Hong Kong expect press freedom, the political system and human rights to deteriorate after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule next year, according to a survey published on Thursday.
The bustling territory returns to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
In a poll conducted by the Better Hong Kong Foundation, 72 percent of respondents expected less press freedom after the handover.
Some 64 percent expected the political system to suffer, and 63 percent saw a deterioration in human rights.

The Better Hong Kong Foundation is a club of leading businessmen formed to promote confidence in Hong Kong ahead of the handover. The survey polled 179 businessmen from last December to August, with a response rate of 31 percent.
Under a Sino-British handover, Hong Kong is guaranteed a high degree of autonomy for 50 years after 1997.
Eighty percent of respondents said they expected corruption to increase after the transfer.
About 74 percent of respondents expected their business in the territory to continue as usual, while others expected to expand or were planning to reassess the situation in 1997.
Seven percent expected to reduce their business presence in Hong Kong or to relocate.
About 65 percent of the respondents expected Hong Kong's economic growth to continue at current levels or increase over the next three years, while one-third expected lower growth.
The government has forecast the real-term growth in the territory's gross domestic product at 4.7 percent this year, after growing 4.6 percent in 1995.
